title: Ola Electric Expands Beyond Scooters With Shakti Energy Storage Push
excerpt: The Indian EV maker is leveraging its gigafactory and 4680 cell technology to enter the ₹1 lakh crore battery energy storage market with a residential product line starting at ₹29,999.
body:
• Ola Electric launched Ola Shakti, a battery energy storage system (BESS) for homes, farms, and small businesses, marking its first non-vehicle product.
  • The product uses Ola's indigenous 4680 Bharat Cell technology manufactured at its Krishnagiri gigafactory in Tamil Nadu, available in four configurations from ₹29,999 to ₹1,59,999.
  • The company expects annual BESS capacity to scale to 5 GWh within the next couple of years, potentially exceeding its automotive consumption.
  • Shakti features IP67-rated weatherproof batteries, instant power changeover, and real-time monitoring through a mobile app.

Ola Electric has entered India's residential battery energy storage market with the launch of Ola Shakti, a portable power solution built on the same cell technology that powers its electric scooters. The move represents the company's first foray beyond vehicles and its bid to capture a share of India's ₹1 lakh crore BESS market.

Bhavish Aggarwal, chairman and managing director of Ola Electric, positioned the product as a natural extension of the company's manufacturing capabilities. "We named it Ola Electric because our long-term vision has always been to build the complete energy ecosystem," Aggarwal said at the launch, according to India Infoline. "India doesn't face an energy shortage; it faces an energy storage opportunity."

From Scooters to Storage

Ola Shakti is powered by the company's in-house 4680 Bharat Cell, the same lithium-ion NMC battery format used in its electric two-wheelers. The product is manufactured at Ola's gigafactory in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, and is available in four configurations: 1 kW/1.5 kWh at ₹29,999, 1 kW/3 kWh at ₹55,999, 3 kW/5.2 kWh at ₹1,19,999, and 6 kW/9.1 kWh at ₹1,59,999.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Bq7wAoXHeoc

According to The Hindu BusinessLine, the system can power air conditioners, refrigerators, induction cookers, farm pumps, and communication equipment, with charging times as fast as two hours and backup capacity of up to 1.5 hours on full load. The batteries carry an IP67 rating, making them resistant to dust, water, and monsoon conditions.

"Ola Shakti is a natural next step for us as we leverage our 4680 cell technology, Gigafactory production capabilities, and nationwide Ola network as a ready sales and distribution backbone."

— Bhavish Aggarwal, Chairman and MD, Ola Electric

Business Case and Profitability

Aggarwal told YourStory that the energy storage business requires "hardly any incremental investment" because it fully leverages Ola's existing two-wheeler platform and manufacturing infrastructure. "The profitability will be actually very good from day one. In our estimate, it will actually be higher than an automotive product also," he said.

The company expects its annual gigafactory consumption for BESS to scale to 5 GWh within the next couple of years, potentially exceeding its automotive consumption, according to YourStory. The pivot toward energy storage has also prompted management to return to its original plan of expanding gigafactory capacity to 20 GWh, Livemint reported.

Ola initially targets the business-to-consumer segment, with B2B container grid products planned for future rollout. The company set a revenue target of ₹100 crore from energy products for the March 2026 quarter, per Livemint.

Market Context for Indian Diaspora

For NRIs with family in India, Ola Shakti addresses a persistent pain point: unreliable grid power and the limitations of traditional lead-acid inverters and diesel generators. Unlike conventional inverters, Shakti operates across a wide input voltage range of 200V-240V, protecting appliances from voltage fluctuations common in many Indian cities and towns.

What's Next

Deliveries of Ola Shakti began from Makar Sankranti 2026, with the product available through the Ola Electric website and Ola Experience Centres. Aggarwal has framed the energy storage business as central to the company's future revenue mix, telling investors that "over the next few quarters, our revenue mix will progressively expand beyond automotive." Whether the aggressive pricing holds up against established inverter brands and new BESS entrants will depend on product reliability and after-sales support — areas where Ola's track record with its scooters has drawn mixed reviews.
